> Preserved P059 planning source. Start with the [current build plan](README.md)
> for the selected Love Burn proposal. Dimensions, depicted equipment, LED
> allocations and delivery status below describe that earlier study; they are
> not current fabrication specifications or fresh supplier quotes.

# Visual and participant modules

These are mutually exclusive visual packages plus optional capture and haze.
The holder's three modeled arms do not establish optical coverage or capacity.
Every fitted device, cover, power pack and cable enters the mass/balance review.
P066 makes one and two heads valid final configurations, including short-throw
heads; three is not a minimum. See the [workbook comparison](../projector-workbook-options.md)
for source prices, smaller-sphere geometry and the remaining $3,000 budget gap.
For an empty optical bench trial, select an accepted test support rather than
assembling an unreviewed occupied lift.

## L0 — LEDs, baseline allocation

1. Define the visible effect and a simple participant/attendant control; choose
   external equipment suited to the actual setting and supply.
2. Test sample light and diffusion on the actual empty sphere/panel. Do not
   apply a coating, adhesive or heat source without material compatibility.
3. Choose the fixture count from the test; the BOM currently carries one kit
   requiring a fixture/cable breakdown rather than invented strip lengths.
4. Fit brackets and secondary retention where required; route power along
   rear/side members, with no cable across the entrance.
5. Record circuit load, switch-off behaviour, temperature and weather protection.
6. Rehearse the participant control and attendant stop before occupied operation.

## P1 — One projector, selected viewing side

1. Borrow/test one standard- or short-throw candidate before committing a purchase. Obtain exact lens
   throw ratio, image aspect, brightness, focus range, ventilation and mounting
   instructions. Old price references are not current purchase quotes.
2. Decide the visible patch; one head is a deliberate single-sided presentation,
   not a 360-degree wrap.
3. Position it on a selected side arm or independent accepted support, avoiding
   the central entry approach; aim onto the sphere with no participant eye beam.
4. Measure actual lens-to-surface distance and patch, focusing at several points
   of the curved target. A centre-to-head distance is not the throw distance.
5. Choose laptop direct HDMI if an existing compatible machine is available;
   verify adapters, cable length, show resolution and playback before buying a node.
6. Add the ventilated rain/salt hood, retention and strain relief; re-check
   balance/temperature and record the added payload.
7. Rehearse default content, restart/power loss and immediate blackout/stop.

## P2 — Two projectors, deliberate partial wrap

1. Complete P1's single-head trial and choose two compatible heads; either
   short- or standard-throw can be evaluated. P2 is a final partial-view option.
2. Mock both positions at their real throws, mapping useful coverage and the
   intentional gaps/entrance sector. Do not claim complete wrap.
3. Compare two side arms against separate accepted stands. Arms preserve the
   one-unit concept; stands add floor area, cable crossings and ballast planning.
4. Verify the output machine can drive two independent desired signals at the
   chosen resolution; account for adapters and software/output configuration.
5. Calibrate per-head mesh, masks and brightness, then test imagery on the
   actual inflated and deformed surface.
6. Fit retained hoods/cables and update structural, electrical and transport totals.
7. Repeat the show/blackout, thermal and empty-to-occupied acceptance sequence.

## P3 — Three short-throw heads on the triangle, modeled upgrade

1. Acquire one short-throw test head or an agreed loan and test focus/coverage
   at the actual geometry. Three purchases are not justified by a render.
2. Check each of the three side/rear corner arms, lens positions and rain covers
   against the chosen device and the clear-front approach. Model arms are 2 m
   at 30 degrees; their tube/wall/joint dimensions are not fabrication specs.
3. Test coverage at 120-degree positions on the curved sphere; map gaps, straps,
   occupant shadows, spill and seams. Three heads alone do not prove 360° coverage.
4. Select a source machine and verified three-output path. Count available ports,
   concurrent resolution/refresh and GPU/adapter limitations, not connector shapes.
5. Have the completed three-arm payload, bending, stays/retention and imbalance
   assessed in both selected ground and lifted modes.
6. Fit three specified mounts, canopies and cable looms, keeping connectors dry
   with their required ventilation and strain relief.
7. Calibrate all three outputs and save a reproducible show preset. Run sustained
   empty tests for focus/temperature and safe stop before occupied rehearsal.
8. Obtain actual quotes for three heads, output hardware and accessories. If
   this does not fit the $3,000 total, retain P1/P2/L0 or secure itemized loans.

## P4 — Four-head coverage study, new mount design required

1. Choose four-head study only if the actual P2/P3 optical trial shows a need.
2. Draw four verified lens positions and coverage; rotating one into the front
   bay is not acceptable. Three triangle corners cannot simply become four.
3. Reviewer designs the fourth support and its reactions/clearances or accepts
   a separate stand outside circulation; update the CAD and parts before fabrication.
4. Verify four real video outputs and synchronisation, then quote the complete
   output/mount/cover/cable package.
5. Re-run the applicable P3 empty coverage, thermal, blackout and payload tests.
6. Reconcile the total budget. This is a deferred optical study, not one of the
   four delivered three-head assemblies or an included Seed purchase package.

## C1 / C2 — One or two participant cameras, optional

1. Start with one available phone/camera; record exact model, ownership,
   battery state, lens and connection. A prior note saying “owned” is not a reservation.
2. Test the required view outside the empty sphere first. Compare an external
   triangle arm through clear skin against an internal position approved for
   the selected sphere; keep entry and seated movement clear.
3. Specify mounts, retention, power-bank and cable containment compatible with
   the sphere/holder. Nothing sharp or hot rests against occupied skin/floor.
4. Test camera feed to the actual laptop/node on the intended local connection,
   with latency, dropouts, exposure and distortion recorded.
5. Implement/test participant consent and an obvious stop control. Use local
   live display with recording off unless a separate informed choice enables it.
6. Compose the live image over moon content; test failure fallback to the moon
   scene rather than freezing a participant's face indefinitely.
7. Add a second camera only when its distinct view helps; C2 replaces C1's count,
   not an additional two cameras. Verify two simultaneous feeds and output load.
8. Repeat actual-location and occupied acceptance after all earlier gates.

Internal cameras are optional and absent from P059's detailed GLBs. The live
overlay cockpit study is a separate concept, not the documented hardware setup.

## H — Owned large external hazer, behind/below the sphere

1. Andrew identifies the actual owned model, fluid, power and manual; acquisition
   cost is zero, while fluid, protection, transport and power remain unpriced.
2. Place it to the rear beneath the sphere's lower edge only if its manual's
   clearance, orientation and ventilation requirements are satisfied. The CAD
   envelope is not the measured unit and rear placement is still provisional.
3. Obtain venue permission and determine weather/power limits. Keep discharge,
   heat and electrical equipment away from the entrance, participant and air intake.
4. Test the effect externally with the sphere empty, minimum useful output and
   an attendant stop; assess visibility, drift and residue on shell/lenses.
5. Confirm the effect does not compromise supervision, footing or electronics;
   include a no-haze show preset and remove the effect when conditions require.
6. Log fluid use, inspect/clean per manual and pack the cooled unit separately.

No hose into the occupied sphere or haze mixed into its inflation air is included
in this build plan. The hazer is an external optional effect, not a blower.
